# Homegate.ch Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/homegate-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/homegate-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Homegate.ch, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Homegate.ch Real Estate Property Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-homegate-ch-real-estate-property-data)
- **Code:** [`homegate.py`](homegate.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/properties.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Homegate property search for finding property listings
- Homagete property pages for property listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_properties(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape listing data from homegate proeprty pages
- `scrape_search(url, scrape_all_pages, max_scrape_pages=10)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape listing data from homegate search pages

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import homegate


async def main():
    properties = await homegate.scrape_properties(
        urls=[
            "https://www.homegate.ch/rent/4002086534",
            "https://www.homegate.ch/rent/4002879785",
        ],
    )
    search = await homegate.scrape_search(
        url="https://www.homegate.ch/rent/real-estate/city-bern/matching-list",
        scrape_all_pages=False,
        max_scrape_pages=2,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/properties.json`](results/properties.json): `localization`, `lister`, `characteristics`, `legacy`, `address`, `externalIds`, `contactForm`, `bfs`, `platforms`, `offerType`, `meta`, `id`, `categories`, `prices`, `valueAddedServices`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `listingType`, `listing`, `listingCard`, `id`, `listingScores`, `listerBranding`, `remoteViewing`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`homegate.py`](homegate.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/homegate-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_properties_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
